examples.en: The wind is coming in, so please close the room door.
The child is waiting in front of the room door.

examples.ko: 방문이 잘 안 열려서 형이 도와줬어요.
examples.en: The room door wouldn't open, so my older brother helped.
My younger sibling stuck a name tag on their own room door.

examples.ko: 방문 손잡이가 고장 나서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: The room door handle is broken, so we have to fix it.
Leave the room door open so the air can pass through.

explain: 그냥 '문'이라고 해도 되지만 '방문'은 방에 달린 문이라고 분명히 말할 때 써요. '현관문', '화장실 문'과 구분되는 말이에요. '방문하다'의 '방문'(visit)과 모양이 같으니 '방문을 닫다/열다'처럼 문과 어울리는 동사로 구별해요.

phrases.en: Someone knocked on my room door, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방에 들어가기 전에 문을 똑똑 칠 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when knocking on a door before entering a room.

explain_en: You can just say '문', but '방문' makes it clear that it is the door of a room, as opposed to '현관문' (front door) or a bathroom door. It looks the same as '방문' (a visit) from '방문하다', so tell them apart by verbs that go with doors, such as '방문을 닫다/열다'.
